title: When the Wolf Burns
premise: Ada Winterbourne, a bone-carver who hears the dead, lives in the valley where magic cannot follow—until a mute child arrives speaking a dead tongue, and the valley's protection shatters. The child is the last citizen of Ysolde, a country unmade by a conqueror's decree, and its people are being erased from memory itself. Pursued by the King's Reckoners, Ada and the child must reassemble Ysolde from scattered bones, graves, and half-remembered songs to find the door out of a nation that officially never existed. In the end, Ada must choose between restoring Ysolde at the cost of her own memories, or letting a country die so its last child can live free; she carves the child's name into her own bone and forgets Ysolde entirely—until the child, grown, returns to carve it back.
about_author: Isandro Villalobos is a former archival restorer who spent a decade cataloguing the belongings of families displaced by border redrawings. He writes fantasy about the paperwork of erasure and the stubbornness of the remembered dead.

chapters.title: Bone Weather
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Ada. Ada carves memorial bones in the valley of Vell Hollow, where magic cannot cross the ridge, and bargains with the dead for quiet. A child appears at her door during a storm, speaking a language no one alive should know. Beat: unease breaking routine.

chapters.title: The Word That Should Not Fit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She tries to place the child with neighbors, but every adult who hears the child's name forgets it moments later. The dead in Ada's bones begin whispering the same word: Ysolde. Beat: dread as the ordinary world starts slipping.

chapters.title: What the Ridge Refuses
chapters.summary: Child's POV, rendered through Ada's translations. The child, Sef, crossed the ridge where magic dies—meaning Sef is carrying something magic cannot bear to touch. First Reckoner scout arrives asking after 'unregistered persons.' Beat: the sanctuary is already compromised.

chapters.title: Grave-Wax and Ledger Ink
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the valley's oldest grave, Ada finds a burial older than the kingdom, marked with Sef's language. The dead woman's memory shows Ysolde whole: cities, songs, a door. Beat: wonder and grief—the country was real, and it is being eaten.

chapters.title: The Reckoners' Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Reckoner Captain Ives's POV. Ives explains the King's Edict of Reconciliation: Ysolde never existed, and its remnants must be collected. He offers Ada amnesty for the child. Beat: chilling bureaucratic menace; the law itself is the antagonist.

chapters.title: Nine Bones of the Founding
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The dead reveal Ysolde's door requires nine founding bones, scattered as relics across the valley and beyond the ridge. Ada, who has never left, decides she must. Sef speaks their first common word: 'hurry.' Beat: commitment; the quest begins.

chapters.title: Crossing Where Magic Dies
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Crossing the ridge, Ada loses her hearing of the dead—the silence is agonizing, like deafness. Sef becomes her interpreter of a world suddenly louder. Beat: vulnerability and dependence; Ada outside her element.

chapters.title: The Market of Almost-Names
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a border town, relics of erased places are sold as trinkets. Ada buys a founding bone with money she doesn't have, owing a debt to a fence who deals in stolen memories. Beat: the cost of the quest becomes personal and financial.

chapters.title: Ives Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Ives's POV. Reckoners burn the market's Ysoltan relics as 'contraband history.' Ives, himself descended from the erased, performs his duty with shaking hands. Beat: antagonist complexity; the law devours even its servants.

chapters.title: The Choir in the Salt Mine
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The third bone lies in a mine where entombed Ysoltan miners still sing. To retrieve it, Ada must join the song—and nearly loses herself in their grief. Sef pulls her out by speaking her mother's name. Beat: the dead as both treasure and trap.

chapters.title: What Sef Remembers
chapters.summary: Sef's POV at last, untranslated. Sef remembers the burning of the archives and being made the 'living ledger'—every erased name pressed into their mind, which is why people forget Sef. Beat: the child's burden revealed; Ada's protectiveness hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Fence's Price
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The memory-fence demands payment: one of Ada's own memories, carved out. Ada surrenders the memory of her father's face to buy the fifth bone. Beat: sacrifice; memory established as currency and wound.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A valley friend who followed them sells their route to the Reckoners to save his own family from 'reconciliation.' Ives takes the fifth bone; Sef is captured. Beat: betrayal and despair at the midpoint's darkest turn.

chapters.title: The Reckoning Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sef is held in a cell of blank paper, where the state literally rewrites prisoners into no one. Ives interrogates Sef and hears, for the first time, a Ysoltan lullaby his grandmother sang. Beat: Ives's loyalty fractures.

chapters.title: Rescue by the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada rallies the dead of the salt mine and the market—everyone the kingdom tried to erase—to overwhelm the Reckoning Room's paper wards. Ives, choosing at last, opens the cell himself. Beat: the theme made flesh; justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Six, Seven, Eight
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A montage of reclamation: a bone pulled from a riverbed, one from a church altar disguised as a saint's finger, one from Ives's own family chest. Each costs Ada a memory. Beat: accelerating momentum shadowed by Ada's erasure.

chapters.title: The Ninth Bone Is a Person
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The ninth founding bone is not an object—it is the last living citizen of the old royal line: Sef. The door out of Ysolde opens only through a willing sacrifice of the ledger itself. Beat: devastating turn; Sef's existence is the key and the price.

chapters.title: The Door That Was a Country
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the buried threshold, the door stands open onto a Ysolde that might be restored whole—requiring Sef to become its keystone, erased into foundation. Ada refuses; Ives arrives with Reckoners to burn the door. Beat: climax converging.

chapters.title: When the Wolf Burns
chapters.summary: Climax, all three POVs. Ada carves the counter-edict into her own arm-bone, using her body as the ninth founding bone: she will forget Ysolde so Sef need not die for it. Ives turns on the Reckoners; the door burns like a wolf's pelt. Beat: self-sacrifice, chaos, fire.

chapters.title: After the Edict
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, fragmented. Ada wakes in Vell Hollow with gaps where a whole country used to be, holding a carved bone she doesn't recognize and a child's coat that smells of smoke. Sef is gone. The dead no longer speak of Ysolde. Beat: hollow victory; grief without an object.

chapters.title: The Name in the Bone
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Years pass. Ada carves again, prosperous and strangely incomplete. One autumn, a grown traveler arrives at her door and begins carving into her memorial bone the name she surrendered: Sef, and with it, Ysolde, returning memory by memory. Beat: tenderness, restoration, chosen family.

chapters.title: Two Countries, One Valley
chapters.summary: Dual POV, coda. Sef, now a keeper of the restored archive-in-exile, settles in the valley where magic cannot follow—making it the one place Ysolde's memory is safe forever. Ada hears the dead singing a new song. Beat: belonging found; memory kept by choice, not law.
